title: Cordon Tolls and Urban Traffic Volumes: Evidence from NYC's 2025 Congestion Relief Zone
abstract: arXiv:2610.34818v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: On January 5, 2025, New York City became the first U.S. city to operate a permanent cordon-based congestion toll, charging vehicles entering Manhattan's Central Business District (the Congestion Relief Zone, or CRZ). This study estimates the short-run causal effect of the toll on hourly traffic volumes using a two-way fixed-effects difference in-differences (TWFE-DiD) strategy that compares treated CRZ street segments to untreated Manhattan segments north of 60th Street. The empirical analysis exploits hourly entry counts from the MTA's toll-meter system (4.86 million ten-minute-block records) as the primary descriptive panel and high-frequency NYC DOT Automated Traffic Recorder (ATR) data as the within-segment identification panel. translated_title: 拥堵收费与城市交通流量：来自纽约市2025年拥堵缓解区的证据
translated_abstract: 2025年1月5日，纽约市成为美国第一个实施永久性基于边界线的拥堵收费政策的城市，对进入曼哈顿中央商务区（即“拥堵缓解区”，CRZ）的车辆征收费用。本研究采用双向固定效应双重差分（TWFE-DiD）策略，将受处理的CRZ街道段与60街以北未受处理的曼哈顿街道段进行比较，估计了该收费对小时交通流量的短期因果效应。实证分析利用大都会运输署（MTA）收费计量系统的每小时进入车辆计数（486万条十分钟区块记录）作为主要描述性面板数据，并使用纽约市交通局（NYC DOT）高频自动交通记录仪（ATR）数据作为段内识别面板。主要的TWFE-DiD点估计结果显示，受处理的CRZ位置的小时对数交通量下降了40%至45%，且该效应方向在九个预注册的替代模型设定中保持一致。
tldr: 本研究利用双重差分方法首次估计了纽约市2025年实施的拥堵收费政策对交通流量的短期因果效应，发现进入曼哈顿中央商务区的小时交通量下降了40%至45%。
en_tdlr: This study provides the first causal estimate of NYC's 2025 congestion toll, finding that cordon pricing reduced hourly traffic volumes entering Manhattan's Central Business District by 40 to 45 percent.
